value.name: letter confirms codicil details
value.description: The letter is read as containing specific references to the codicil and the filing location without contradicting Mrs. Adelman's account.
evidence: It mentioned the codicil by name. It said where the original was meant to be filed. It did not say anything that contradicted what Mrs. Adelman had told her on the phone.

value.name: Asha reviews the letter
value.description: Asha folds the letter back into its envelope and pauses with it in her hands, considering its significance.
evidence: Asha folded the letter back into its envelope and held it in both hands for a moment.

value.name: Asha distinguishes evidence from codicil
value.description: Asha explains to Lucia that the letter shows intent and corroborates witnesses, but is not itself a valid codicil.
evidence: "Lucia," she said. "This is evidence of intent. It is not, by itself, a codicil. A holographic instrument in Pennsylvania has to meet certain requirements, and this letter is not trying to be a will. It does corroborate Mrs. Adelman and Rosa. It corroborates them strongly."

value.name: Lucia confirms need for codicil
value.description: Lucia acknowledges that the legal team still needs the actual codicil document.
evidence: "So we still need the codicil itself."

value.name: Asha explains fallback legal strategy
value.description: Asha says the successor firm is searching for the original and outlines a harder, slower argument if it cannot be found.
evidence: "Ideally. The successor firm is searching. If the original cannot be found, there are arguments I can make based on the witness testimony and this letter, but they are harder, and they will be uglier, and they will take longer, and the longer they take the more the estate bleeds. I would like to find the document."

value.name: Lucia asks about failure case
value.description: Lucia presses Asha on what happens if the codicil cannot be found.

value.name: Asha leaves decision to Lucia
value.description: Asha tells Lucia that choosing the harder legal argument will be Lucia's decision, though Asha will advise her.
evidence: "Then we will have a conversation about whether you want to make the harder argument. That will be your call. I will tell you what I think. But I will not make it for you."

value.name: Lucia appears exhausted
value.description: Lucia silently accepts the explanation and looks very tired while Rosa watches from the doorway.
evidence: Lucia nodded. She looked very tired. Rosa, in the doorway, was watching them both with an expression Asha could not quite read.

value.name: Asha begins another warning
value.description: Asha introduces one more important matter and starts to tell Lucia something she needs to know.
